proposed.comparator_claim: Discrete causal bounds can be computed as polynomial programs with convergent anytime outer bounds.
Finite causal response-type models can have complete observable facet inequalities beyond Pearl's basic instrumental inequality.
A deterministic parent map supports duplicate-free reverse-search enumeration without storing visited objects.

Two-arm ordinal benefit probabilities have sharp cumulative formulas for unrestricted bivariate potential-outcome couplings; those formulas do not transfer sharply to the three-way non-valley support restriction.
Two-potential-outcome distributional bounds under support restrictions admit a Kantorovich-dual characterization.

Arbitrary-objective multi-marginal transport can represent the present legal-support problem after an explicit extended-cost encoding of illegal cells; the paper's quadratic-objective plug-in rate does not transfer to the unique-peak indicator, for which the present work proves an equivalent finite legal-incidence program directly.

Their compatibility graph concerns observable implications of potential-response support restrictions and requires every maximal clique to correspond to a support point.  Here every two-dose projection is full, so the graph is complete tripartite and every triple is a maximal three-clique, including the deleted strict-middle valleys; that premise fails, and the present polytope additionally augments arm marginals by three unique-peak target coordinates.
Randomly perturbed LP value functions yield uniformly valid confidence sets for linear functionals of set-identified parameters.
For Gaussian first-stage limits, ordinary bootstrap consistency is equivalent to full differentiability, and a derivative-estimation bootstrap handles directional maps.
Intersection bounds admit adaptive inequality selection and Gaussian-process inference.
Continuous functionals of the joint distribution of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model admit sharp bounds through random-set restrictions and convex optimization.

For binary treatment and an ordinal outcome, exact randomization inference in the paper assumes independent potential outcomes and concerns the relative treatment effect, not the present three-dose unique-best endpoint map.

Sharp symbolic ordinal bounds are derived for binary-exposure observational confounding and binary-instrument noncompliance designs; they do not classify or evaluate a three-dose forbidden-support unique-best polytope.

prose_updates.tldr: Randomization identifies the three marginals of a prespecified ordinal benefit-risk score but not the population shares for which each dose is uniquely best.  Under weak individual unimodality, the compatible target vectors form a structured three-marginal polytope.  The staircase family with \(3^{L-3}\) weighted facets, the exact small-support counts \(59\), \(197\), and \(721\), and sharp endpoint formulas using at most three full facets are proved.  Independently of any all-support facet stream, a finite legal-incidence program computes all six scalar endpoints exactly in polynomial time for rational input, constructs endpoint-attaining rational mixtures with support at most \(3L-2\), and the \(L=2\) equal-Bernoulli example proves that this support bound is uniformly sharp.  Fixed-\(L\) plug-in rates and exact finite-sample simultaneous endpoint coverage, including zero cells and realized empty arms, are also proved.  The remaining mathematical questions are the all-\(L\) exact-once stream with its finite predecessor and transfer classification, and regular-face equivalence of the exact scalar procedure to a specified efficient Wald interval.  The Goodwin et al. application remains an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis: the trial identifies score marginals but neither identifies nor clinically validates weak individual unimodality.

project_justification.gap: Existing two-dose results sharply bound functionals of two potential outcomes, and generic discrete causal or multi-marginal optimizers can return numerical bounds.  The cited two-potential-outcome and generic optimization works do not study the paper-specific task of classifying \(\mathcal H_L\) by a finite predecessor map satisfying \(\mathsf{CHECK}_{2\mathrm{BTAS}}\).  Kaido and Ponomarev's maximal-clique correspondence does not cover this support: all two-dose projections are full, making the potential-response graph complete tripartite and every triple a maximal three-clique, including the deleted strict-middle valleys.  Their graph describes observable support implications, whereas \(Q_{3,L}\) also augments randomized marginals by the three unique-peak target coordinates.
project_justification.fill: The proved layer gives an exponential staircase facet family, exact catalogues for \(L\le5\), three-facet sharp endpoint formulas, exact polynomial-time scalar evaluation for rational inputs, sparse endpoint-attaining mixtures, a fixed-\(L\) plug-in rate, and finite-sample simultaneous endpoint honesty.  The open combinatorial layer asks for a finite renormalized predecessor classification and a literal \(\texttt{CHECK\_2BTAS}\)-accepted source whose soundness, completeness, and uniqueness hold for every \(L\).  Separately, regular-face Wald equivalence of the already honest exact scalar interval remains open.

prose_updates.related_work: Russell (2021) studies sharp bounds for continuous functionals of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model through random-set restrictions and convex optimization.  Chiba (2017) studies the binary-treatment ordinal relative-treatment-effect parameter and gives exact randomization inference under independent potential outcomes.  Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) derive sharp cumulative formulas and attaining tables for unrestricted bivariate ordinal couplings.  Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) derive symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds for binary-exposure confounding and binary-instrument noncompliance designs.  None of these two-potential-outcome results transfers sharply to the present three-way forbidden support.  Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) give an arbitrary-objective multi-marginal transport architecture that can encode illegal cells by extended cost, but their quadratic-objective plug-in rate does not transfer to the indicator endpoint; the present legal-incidence linear program, exact separator, and rational polynomial-time computation are proved directly.  Finite linear-programming strong duality is used in the exact form of Trevisan (2011, Lecture 6, Theorem 6.5), while polynomial-time rational linear programming is drawn from Lecture 5, Section 2.4.  Kaido and Ponomarev (2025) characterize observable implications of support restrictions by compatibility graphs under a maximal-clique correspondence.  Every two-dose projection here is full, so the potential-response graph is complete tripartite and every triple is a maximal three-clique, including the strict-middle valleys deleted from \(\mathcal U_L\); consequently their requirement that every maximal clique correspond to a support point fails.  Their graph concerns observable support implications, whereas \(Q_{3,L}\) additionally carries the three unique-peak target coordinates.  Duarte et al. (2024) provide generic polynomial-program bounds, Bonet (2001) provides a causal-facet precedent, and Avis and Fukuda (1996) motivate duplicate-free predecessor enumeration, but none supplies the paper-specific finite predecessor map.  Cho and Russell (2024), Fang and Santos (2019), and Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013) motivate perturbation and intersection-bound inference.  Here exact finite-sample simultaneous honesty and a fixed-\(L\) plug-in rate are proved; only regular-face Wald equivalence remains open.  Goodwin et al. (2022) provide the randomized three-dose setting, used solely for an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis under a prespecified score and an added, clinically unvalidated cross-world unimodality restriction.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The staircase family and the exact catalogues through \(L=5\) are proved, but they do not furnish the finite predecessor type set or an accepted all-\(L\) source.  In particular, the direct two-register encoding of alternating \(\mathrm L\) and \(\mathrm R\) staircase updates violates a fixed triangular order; a different representation within sixteen registers or an impossibility proof is still required.  Scalar endpoint formulas, polynomial-time rational computation, sparse attaining mixtures, fixed-\(L\) plug-in rates, and exact finite-sample simultaneous honesty do not depend on resolving that stream.  The only remaining inference issue is the uniform local normal and quantile approximation needed to prove regular-face Wald equivalence under the procedure's simultaneous error allocation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved results are the all-\(L\) staircase facet family, exact facet counts \(F_2=7\), \(F_3=59\), \(F_4=197\), and \(F_5=721\), sharp scalar endpoint formulas using at most three full facets, exact polynomial-time rational endpoint computation, endpoint-attaining rational mixtures with support at most \(3L-2\), the sharpness of that support bound at \(L=2\), the fixed-\(L\) plug-in rate, and exact finite-sample simultaneous endpoint honesty.  These endpoint and inference results are independent of the unresolved facet stream.  Open claims are confined to the existence or impossibility of one exact-once all-\(L\) two-pass stream with a finite predecessor and transfer classification, and to regular-face equivalence between the exact scalar interval and a semiparametrically efficient Wald interval with an explicitly matched critical value.  No scalar efficiency claim is made.  The Goodwin et al. use case is an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis based on the prespecified score: random assignment and consistency identify arm marginals, but the trial neither identifies nor clinically validates weak individual unimodality, and no data analysis or empirical verification of that restriction is claimed.
